name: tab-to-search-scope-chip
description:
Tab-to-search. The Swift bar scoped the palette to a search engine and showed a chip naming it; the HTML palette that replaced it handled no Tab key at all.

The engine has to come from the PROFILE, not from a literal in the page. Chromium's AutocompleteController attaches a match's associated_keyword when the typed text resolves to a TemplateURL keyword, so the scenario types a whole keyword - 'bing.com' - rather than a prefix of one: KeywordProvider::GetTemplateUrlForText looks the text up as a keyword, it does not complete it. Bing is prepopulated in every region Chromium ships, and seed_prefs pins Google as the DEFAULT so the row's engine is a non-default one and the offer is a real choice.

WHAT A FAILURE HERE MEANS. 'scope-offers-before-tab' is read before the Tab key and answers the question the chip assertions cannot: a profile whose TemplateURLService never loaded an engine and a Tab key the page dropped both leave the chip empty, and only this count tells them apart. It reads data-cb-keyword, which the page puts on a row for exactly that reason.

The fixture is a sibling scenario's, reused unchanged: this measures the palette, and two restored tabs are only a way to know the app is up. Nothing here depends on the tabs themselves.

NOT CLAIMED: that Enter inside the scope reaches the engine's results page. That needs a live network and a settled suggest pass, and the accept path is the ordinary commandBarAccept one the page tests already pin.

assertions.desc: the typed keyword resolved to a TemplateURL and exactly one row carries it - UpdateAssociatedKeywords dedupes, so a second row offering the same engine would be a bug. A zero here says the profile has no engine to scope to and every chip assertion below is measuring the wrong thing.
and it is the engine the typed text names, so the count above is not one of something else
the field row names the engine Tab would scope to, before Tab is pressed
Tab entered the scope and the chip carries the engine's DISPLAY name, which only TemplateURLService knows - the keyword alone would read 'bing.com'
The field cleared. Without this the chip could be showing over the text that summoned it
the hint yields to the chip once the scope is entered
the scope survives typing. A chip that vanished on the first keystroke would satisfy every other assertion here
Escape restored the pre-Tab text rather than the 'hats' typed inside the scope, and the palette stayed open to be read at all
And the scope is gone with it - the chip element is removed, so the eval's fallback is what reads
